native_result.query: How is the advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students related to Socioeconomic status levels?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students is more pronounced at lower SES levels with the interaction term for Socioeconomic status and being black having a coefficient of 0.7606
native_result.HypoB: The Black-non-Hispanic-white advantage in college-degree-track/completed education is NOT a low-SES Black advantage: among NLSY79 respondents aged 20+ (near-final education), the Black-minus-NBNH any-college (>=13 yrs) completion gap is ~0 at low SES (-0.2pp), positive and significant only at MIDDLE SES (+10.6pp, 95% CI 0.5-20.7pp), and ~<=0 at high SES (-2.5pp); continuous years of schooling show the LARGEST Black deficit at low SES (~-1.0 yr, p<0.001). The relationship between any Black completion advantage and SES is non-monotonic (hump-shaped, centered at mid SES) and reflects college-entry rather than BA-degree completion, which is essentially unobservable in this file (HG>=16 cells: Black 2/296, 0/97, 2/64; NBNH 4/602, 5/952, 19/781).
native_result.WorkflowB: Load data/nls_raw.csv (12,686x61). Clean: HG79 (95->missing), outcomes BA(>=16, descriptive) and any-college(>=13) and continuous HG79; cohort BLACK(1) vs NBNH(3); SES composite z = mean of standardized log(income1979+1), mother ed, father ed; pooled tertiles (cutoffs -0.211, 0.330); covariates age, sex. Analyses: stratified rates & Black-minus-NBNH gaps (Wald CI) per SES level, full and age>=20; logistic (any-college) and OLS (HG79) with Black*C(ses)+age+male, reporting AME gaps per SES and interaction p; bootstrap (B=1000) CI for age>=20 headline gaps. Robustness: SES single-indicator (income-only; mother-ed-only), within-race tertile cutoffs, MICE-lite (5 imputations of loginc/moth/fath, chained regression), Hispanic-inclusive comparison (Black vs all non-Black), ASVAB-avg (+rel class rank) covariates, 1989 savings-direction covariate & interaction, adult-wealth (1985/1996) alternative SES. Diagnostics: per-cell n reported throughout; missingness carried into write-up (income-1979 19.6%, wealth-1996 44.5%, savings amount 79.3%, rank-in-class 55.4%, etc.). All deterministic (seed 42); script analysis.py; output log analysis_output.txt.

sub_hypo.text: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students is more pronounced at lower socioeconomic status levels, with a coefficient of 0.7606 for the interaction between socioeconomic status and being Black.
sub_hypo.context: Students in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79), with emphasis on lower socioeconomic status levels.
variables: BA degree completion (no explicit column specified)
sub_hypo.relations: Socioeconomic status moderates the association between being Black and BA degree completion: the advantage for Black students is more pronounced at lower SES levels. The SES × Black interaction coefficient is 0.7606.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students is more pronounced at lower SES levels with the interaction term for Socioeconomic status and being black having a coefficient of 0.7606

sub_hypo.text: Among NLSY79 respondents aged 20 or older, the Black-minus-non-Black-non-Hispanic any-college gap is approximately zero at low SES, positive and significant only at middle SES, and slightly negative at high SES, producing a hump-shaped rather than a low-SES Black advantage.
sub_hypo.context: Black and non-Black non-Hispanic NLSY79 respondents aged at least 20 in 1979, representing near-final education. SES is the mean of standardized log(income1979+1), mother's education, and father's education, divided into pooled tertiles at -0.211 and 0.330. Models adjust for age and sex.
variables: Total net family income, previous calendar year, 1979
Highest grade completed by respondent's mother, 1979
Highest grade completed by respondent's father, 1979
sub_hypo.relations: Any college is defined as highest grade completed >=13, with 95 treated as missing. Black-minus-NBNH gaps are -0.2 percentage points at low SES, +10.6 points at middle SES (95% CI 0.5–20.7), and -2.5 points at high SES. The racial gap varies non-monotonically with SES, peaking at middle SES.

sub_hypo.text: Among NLSY79 respondents aged 20 or older, continuous years of schooling show the largest Black deficit relative to non-Black non-Hispanic respondents at low SES.
sub_hypo.context: Black and non-Black non-Hispanic NLSY79 respondents aged at least 20 in 1979. SES uses pooled tertiles of the composite of standardized log(income1979+1), mother's education, and father's education, with cutoffs -0.211 and 0.330. OLS models adjust for age and sex.
variables: Total net family income, previous calendar year, 1979
Highest grade completed by respondent's mother, 1979
Highest grade completed by respondent's father, 1979
sub_hypo.relations: The Black-minus-NBNH difference in continuous highest grade completed is most negative at low SES, approximately -1.0 year (p<0.001), contradicting a low-SES Black educational advantage.

sub_hypo.text: The middle-SES Black any-college advantage reflects college entry rather than BA-degree completion, which is essentially unobservable because BA-completion cells are extremely sparse.
sub_hypo.context: Black and non-Black non-Hispanic NLSY79 respondents aged at least 20 in 1979, compared across low, middle, and high pooled SES tertiles defined by the income-and-parental-education composite.
variables: Total net family income, previous calendar year, 1979
Highest grade completed by respondent's mother, 1979

sub_hypo.relations: Highest grade completed >=13 indicates any college, not BA completion; >=16 is the descriptive BA threshold. Across low, middle, and high SES, respectively, BA counts are 2/296, 0/97, and 2/64 for Black respondents versus 4/602, 5/952, and 19/781 for NBNH respondents. These sparse cells do not establish a Black BA-completion advantage.

Malformed judge output raises an evaluation error; no hidden retries.
evaluator_config.aggregation: recall_context * mean_accuracy_score; unmatched predicted contexts stay in denominator
evaluator_config.native_behavior_preserved: Variable/relation comparisons receive full hypotheses for each matched context pair.

details.score_scope: Reference agreement of submitted hypothesis; execution is not independently verified by this native metric.
